title: Remove repeated strategy-table scans from Paper settlement retention lookup
author: agent:/root

scope.goal: First bounded correction of the accepted settlement-persistence latency issue: provide an index for the verified repeated strategy-wallet equality lookup, without changing settlement or retention behavior.
inScope: One new nonunique HASH expression index public.ix_strategies_retention_wallet_lookup on public.strategies using exactly lower('strategy:' || code), with the existing expression collation and no predicate, included columns, uniqueness or code-length restriction.

New ordered migration 0009-strategy-retention-wallet-index at order8, registered in the existing migration catalog. CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY outside a transaction, exact completion validation and the existing migration ledger protocol. Immutable baseline and all eight existing migration SQL/checksums remain unchanged.

An optional per-migration command timeout in the existing migration model and pending-SQL execution path, set to60seconds only for the new migration. Existing migrations retain their current timeout and checksum behavior. No migration-framework redesign.

Focused migration, lookup, retention and settlement regression tests plus a short README deployment/limitation note. Builds/tests may use the installed PostgreSQL17 runtime in a dedicated disposable instance under a marked D:\CodexTemp run, not the user's application Local database. Production18.3 is not represented as locally integration-tested.
Local source changes only after later exact-digest approval. User controls deployment. This contract does not authorize the agent to create the index or alter the migration ledger on Production.
outOfScope: Changing any lookup SQL, retention function/trigger, restoration guard, advisory/row lock, transaction boundary, retry, queue, worker, settlement processor or position-upsert semantics.
Changing strategies, strategy codes, execution intents, Paper/Live orders/fills, accounting, fees, balances, historical records or Maker-GTD classification.
Copied-performance projection, Dashboard, Binance/SOL freshness or other improvement workstreams; new telemetry or generalized migration/recovery infrastructure.

Production mutation, agent manual index application, Production/application Local ANALYZE/VACUUM, backup, deployment, service stop/restart, server configuration or software installation. No automatic DROP/REINDEX or bypass of failed migration checks. Isolated test-fixture index application and ANALYZE remain allowed for the specified verification.

requirements.text: Make the existing case-insensitive strategy-wallet equality lookup indexable without changing its matching, ordering or retention behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: The only new application-schema object is public.ix_strategies_retention_wallet_lookup: nonunique HASH, one key lower('strategy:' || code), default existing collation/operator class, no partial predicate or INCLUDE. Existing ORDER BY strategy.id remains in the original function; hash ordering or index-only execution is not assumed.

New migration0009/order8 has a fixed SQL checksum and an exact pg_catalog completion check including intended table/schema/expression/access method, valid/ready/live, nonunique status and absence of additional keys/predicate. A pre-existing correct index is accepted without rebuilding; wrong/invalid same-name objects are rejected without a success ledger row or automatic destructive recovery.
The immutable baseline and all eight existing migration definitions/checksums remain unchanged. Default-catalog count and second-start ledger tests reflect exactly one additional migration.

Identical ordered UUID results before/after the index for ordinary, mixed-case, multiple case-variant codes, missing/non-strategy/empty/null wallet inputs, empty code, representative non-ASCII text under the same collation and long-code fixtures. A verified pair of distinct folded values with the same hash must still be distinguished by the unchanged equality predicate; no truncation, uniqueness or new maximum code length.

A representative synthetic fixture demonstrates natural planner use of the new index with literal, prepared custom and prepared generic queries; report plans/buffers before/after and statistics availability. Do not use enable_seqscan=off as sole performance proof. Isolated fixture ANALYZE is allowed for verification only; no Production ANALYZE is authorized. Production speedup remains unconfirmed until a later read-only post-deployment check.

requirements.text: Bound only the new migration command while preserving existing startup and failure semantics, with deployment risks made explicit.
acceptanceCriteria: Optional positive CommandTimeoutSeconds is appended source-compatibly to PostgresSchemaMigration; null preserves current behavior. Pending migration SQL uses the explicit value when supplied. Only0009 specifies60seconds; existing migration SQL timeouts remain0 and metadata/history commands remain15seconds. Baseline bootstrap is unchanged.

Existing normalized-SQL-only checksum calculation remains unchanged, including for the new SQL. The60second timeout is enforced by catalog/configuration tests and this requirement contract, not misrepresented as a new ledger-checksum format.

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY executes as one standalone command outside an explicit or implicit multi-statement transaction. Exact completion is checked before the existing short ledger transaction. No row-history batching, broad table lock, retry loop, trigger bypass or service-control mechanism is added.

Cancellation/timeout/error records no migration success and propagates the existing startup failure. A cancelled concurrent build may leave an invalid index; it is not silently dropped/repaired. The command timeout is not a promise of an exact60second end-to-end startup deadline. Test cancellation and connection/migration-lock release using a short synthetic timeout instead of a60second sleep.

README explicitly states that user deployment applies this migration at startup; a blocker/error/invalid index can prevent startup and needs separate approved intervention. Concurrent construction avoids locking out ordinary table writes but may wait for existing transactions and adds temporary CPU/I/O load. Existing old binaries reject an unknown0009 ledger row on restart: no promise of blind rollback to538c726c after migration.

No agent Production DDL or ledger write occurs under this source-only contract. Any separately requested operational application first needs a fresh read-only preview of exact index/table, strategy count, service state, blockers and progress state. Durable states are pg_index readiness/validity then the existing schema-migration ledger; invalid state is a stop, not an automatic resume/rebuild.
